question: Which of the following best describes the text's overall structure? In Karuk—an Indigenous language of the West Coast in what is today the United States—the word ihmar translates to "to run," while the related word ihmáraramnih translates to "to run into." When a portion of a root word recurs, sometimes in a modified form, inside another word tied to that root, the process is known as reduplication. Here, the piece "ar" found in ihmar reappears in ihmáraramnih, and Karuk offers many such examples of reduplication.
option a: It defines the process of reduplication, notes the scholarly controversy surrounding it, and then argues that examining Karuk might resolve that controversy.
option b: It outlines how Karuk relates to several other languages, poses a question about that relationship, and then answers it.
option c: It offers particular words from Karuk, identifies the broad linguistic process those words illustrate, and then observes that the process is common in Karuk.
option d: It points out the words used most often in Karuk, explains the difficulty of translating them into English, and then names other languages into which they can be rendered.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text gives specific Karuk words, names the general phenomenon (reduplication), then notes it occurs often in Karuk.

question: Based on the two texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely react to the underlined claim in Text 1? Text 1: The poetry of John Clare, capturing both the beauty and the hardship of rural England in the nineteenth century, shows that a convincing poetic rendering of nature has to rest on the authenticity of ordinary lived experience. A tenant farmer who taught himself to write poetry, Clare produced verse steeped in the rhythms of farming life—something apparent in "The Shepherd's Calendar," which paints the shifting seasons and the everyday routines of country living. Text 2: Like numerous other poets of the Romantic era, Samuel Taylor Coleridge admired nature from a distance. His verse frequently renders ordinary landscapes in a mystical, awe-filled manner, prompting readers to perceive nature's grandeur and to share his reverence for it. "Frost at Midnight" illustrates this approach, as the poet draws on the stillness of a winter night to reflect on nature's beauty and its link to human thought.
option a: By challenging the notion that poetic depictions of nature not rooted in genuine everyday experience are ineffective.
option b: By maintaining that profound admiration of nature can likewise strengthen the authenticity of how it is portrayed in poetry.
option c: By arguing that authentic poetic portrayals of nature arise from experiencing natural settings alongside other people.
option d: By suggesting that authentic poetic portrayals of nature call for a balance between lived experience and poetic imagination.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Text 2 praises Coleridge's distant, imaginative view of nature, so its author would dispute the claim that such non-firsthand depictions are ineffective.

question: Which choice best expresses the main idea of the text? The prolific career of Mexican architect Luis Barragán, stretching from the 1920s into the 1980s, moved through clearly separate phases. Having traveled to the United States and Europe in the early 1930s and steeped himself in an international conversation about architecture, Barragán started applying ideas drawn from functionalism and modernism, as the Chávez Peón de Ochoa House demonstrates; its plain geometric shapes stand in contrast to the historically inspired style of the Aguilar House, one of his early works in Guadalajara.
option a: Barragán's Chávez Peón de Ochoa House and Aguilar House are regarded as models of a functionalist and modernist aesthetic.
option b: Barragán's early work reveals a first commitment to a modernist aesthetic that he later gave up.
option c: A marked change in Barragán's design aesthetic reflects the impact of his time overseas.
option d: Barragán's design of the Aguilar House is viewed as more experimental than his design of the Chávez Peón de Ochoa House.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage centers on how travel abroad shifted Barragán's aesthetic toward functionalism and modernism.

question: Which choice best expresses the main idea of the text? The passage below comes from Ralph Waldo Emerson's 1841 essay "The Method of Nature." The swift fortunes that hundreds in the community gain through trade, or through the ceaseless growth of our population and industries, dazzle everyone else; one person's good luck becomes the hope of thousands, and the lure works like a nearby gold mine that drains the farm, the school, the church, the household, and even the body and features of a person.
option a: People who want to build wealth can do so faster through trade than through pursuits such as teaching and farming.
option b: Taking part in a range of activities matters for a person's physical health.
option c: When a handful of people in a society grow wealthy, the rest of society will, in time, benefit as well.
option d: Watching a few people succeed can drive many to give up important parts of their own lives while chasing comparable success.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Emerson warns that the lure of others' rapid wealth drains the farm, school, church, and home as people chase the same success.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the student's conclusion? Average Hours Worked per Person per Year in 1950 and 2017. Country / 1950 / 2017 / Change in hours / Percent change in hours: Brazil, 2,042, 1,709, -333, -16%; Denmark, 2,049, 1,400, -649, -32%; Austria, 2,086, 1,613, -473, -23%; Peru, 2,157, 1,932, -225, -10%. Figures may not be exact because of rounding. For an economics course, a student is looking into the drop since 1950 in the average number of hours each person works per year across several countries, a drop attributed both to higher productivity and to the introduction of policies capping working hours. The student's first goal is to see how Brazil's decline stacks up against the declines in the other countries, and the student determines that ______
option a: although Brazil's drop in hours worked was smaller than Denmark's and Austria's, it was larger than Peru's.
option b: although Brazil's drop in hours worked was larger than Denmark's and Peru's, it was smaller than Austria's.
option c: while the number of hours worked increased in Brazil between 1950 and 2017, it fell in Denmark, Austria, and Peru.
option d: the percent decrease in hours worked was larger in Brazil than in Denmark, Austria, or Peru.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Brazil's 333-hour drop is smaller than Denmark's 649 and Austria's 473 but larger than Peru's 225.

question: Which quotation from a literary critic would best support the text's claim about critics? Bruce Sterling's 1986 cyberpunk collection Mirrorshades includes only twelve carefully chosen stories, and by the close of the 1980s Sterling himself declared that cyberpunk—a subgenre of science fiction—was an artistic movement that had died. Editor Jared Shurin's 2023 anthology The Big Book of Cyberpunk, however, ranges widely across time and contains 108 stories, among them Fritz Leiber's "Coming Attraction" (1950) and Yudhanjaya Wijeratne's "The State Machine" (2020). Critics have argued that, when it comes to method of publication, Shurin's sense of what counts as a cyberpunk short story is far broader than Sterling's.
option a: "Whatever its strengths, Mirrorshades overlooked certain strands of cyberpunk that would later shape science fiction as a whole, mainly because Sterling limited himself to short stories written within a narrow span of time (the early 1980s)."
option b: "Many of the finest science fiction writers work only in the short story form. Anthologies such as The Big Book of Cyberpunk perform a vital role for them, bringing their work to the many readers who buy stand-alone books but seldom pick up science fiction magazines or online journals."
option c: "Unlike the pieces in Mirrorshades, not every story gathered in The Big Book of Cyberpunk first appeared in a print publication: qntm's 2021 story 'Lena,' for instance, was originally self-published on the author's site qntm.org."
option d: "In contrast to Sterling, who frames cyberpunk as a period-bound broadening of science fiction's limits, Shurin frames it as a genre with fixed conventions and essential traits unconnected to those of science fiction."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only option C addresses method of publication, contrasting print-only Mirrorshades with a self-published story in Shurin's anthology.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? People taking part in a study of musical perception gave high groove ratings—groove being how strongly one is drawn to move to a song—to Earth, Wind & Fire's "Boogie Wonderland." In a separate study, participants gave comparably high groove ratings to the Brazilian samba tune "Desafinado." If, as some maintain, a person's sense of groove relies on the capacity to "find the pulse" (grasp the steady underlying rhythm) of a song, then it would follow that participants in these two studies tended to ______
option a: find the pulses of their respective songs easily.
option b: perceive their respective songs as rhythmically complex.
option c: experience little desire to move to their respective songs.
option d: rate the pulses of their respective songs rather than the grooves.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If high groove requires finding the pulse, then the high ratings imply the listeners located the pulse easily.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? A 2018 study by Deepak Jaiswal and Rishi Kant reported that how much consumers knew about environmental issues made no difference to how likely they were to buy environmentally friendly products. Because that study drew on fewer than 400 young adults in India, though, questions have arisen about how reliable and representative its results are. Seeking a clearer picture, Wencan Zhuang and colleagues examined the findings of 54 studies of eco-friendly consumer behavior—among them a 2014 study from China with 909 participants and a 2015 study from India with 270 participants. Considering all 54 studies together, Zhuang and colleagues detected a significant positive effect of environmental knowledge on eco-friendly purchasing choices, which suggests that ______
option a: the number of participants in Jaiswal and Kant's study was far below the number in most studies of purchasing decisions.
option b: the participants in Jaiswal and Kant's study may not have been representative of consumers in general regarding environmentally friendly purchasing decisions.
option c: a sample of 270 people may be enough to draw reliable conclusions about the link between knowledge of environmental issues and purchasing decisions.
option d: Jaiswal and Kant's methodology was more precise than that used in the 2014 study from China.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because the pooled 54 studies found a positive effect that Jaiswal and Kant's narrow sample did not, their participants were likely unrepresentative.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In 2013, Shirley Ann Williams et al. carried out a meta-analysis (a review of earlier research) of studies concerning the social media site now known as Twitter—such as the 2011 paper by Bollen et al., "Happiness Is Assortative in Online Social Networks"—in order to spot trends in the research. Williams's team found that although a sizable number of papers concentrated on user profiles, many concentrated on the content of messages. The team also found that researchers focusing on message content were especially inclined to rely on knowledge discovery methods (techniques rooted in statistical analysis and artificial intelligence designed to process huge quantities of information), which suggests that ______
option a: knowledge discovery methods produce less reliable results when applied to user profiles than to the content of social media messages.
option b: researchers usually assumed that a small share of users accounts for most of the information in social media messages.
option c: researchers tended to anticipate that the amount of information in social media messages would be particularly large.
option d: studies that use knowledge discovery methods are cited more widely than studies that do not.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since knowledge discovery methods handle enormous amounts of information, using them for message content implies researchers expected that content to hold especially large amounts of information.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Katy Milkman, a behavioral economist at the University of Pennsylvania, investigates how psychological factors—emotion and bias among them—shape the economic decisions that individuals ______ Milkman's work also weighs the wider effects these decisions have on the economy.
option a: make; moreover,
option b: make, moreover;
option c: make, moreover,
option d: make, moreover.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon separates the two independent clauses, and the comma follows the transitional word "moreover."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? When it was released in 1999, the Intel Pentium III microchip held just one CPU, or core, for carrying out commands. Since that time, the average processing power of microchips has ______ cores now reach into the dozens, hundreds, or even thousands—that the once-revolutionary dual-core technology that succeeded the single-core chip now turns up in everyday objects such as toasters and toothbrushes.
option a: increased--so drastically,
option b: increased so drastically,
option c: increased so drastically--
option d: increased, so drastically,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash after "drastically" sets off the parenthetical clause that pairs with the later dash.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? At the Rankin Inlet observatory in Canada, radars aim their antennae skyward to track gravity waves and other geospace phenomena. These radars are not the only ones surveying the ______ over thirty additional radar sites across the globe watch these very phenomena as part of the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network.
option a: sky, though,
option b: sky, though;
option c: sky though
option d: sky; though,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon joins the two independent clauses, and the comma follows the transitional "though."

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Within a chemical equation, the quantity called molar mass helps in converting between the mass of the reactants and the mass of the product. The gaseous ______ have molar masses of 48.00 and 56.11 g/mol, respectively.
option a: compounds ozone (O3) and isobutylene (C4H8),
option b: compounds, ozone (O3) and isobutylene (C4H8)
option c: compounds ozone (O3) and isobutylene (C4H8)
option d: compounds, ozone (O3) and isobutylene (C4H8),
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation is needed around the essential appositive naming the two compounds.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Karl Popper's contention that scientific hypotheses must be capable of being disproved in theory—known as the criterion of falsifiability—rejects the confirmationist ______ verifiability as the crucial criterion for scientific hypotheses. For Popper, a statement such as "all spiders have eight legs" counts as scientific not because it can be verified, or shown to be true, but because it can in theory be shown to be false.
option a: argument, it posits
option b: argument positing
option c: argument and posits
option d: argument, positing
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The participial phrase "positing verifiability..." attaches to "argument" without punctuation, avoiding a comma splice or run-on.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The visual magnitude scale, a measure of stellar brightness, runs on a reverse logarithmic basis: the brighter a star, the smaller its magnitude number. ______ Gamma Velorum, the 30th-brightest star in the sky, carries a higher visual magnitude number (1.72) than the brighter star Aldebaran does. Aldebaran, the 14th-brightest star, has a magnitude of 0.86.
option a: On the other hand,
option b: Nonetheless,
option c: Moreover,
option d: Hence,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The Gamma Velorum example follows as a consequence of the reverse-logarithmic rule, so "Hence" fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The total solar eclipse of April 6, 648 BCE, inspired a well-known poem written that same year by the Greek lyric poet Archilochus. Another notable solar eclipse took place on October 22, 2137 BCE, but unlike the eclipse of 648 BCE, the one in 2137 BCE was annular. ______ the Moon did not blot out the Sun entirely, leaving instead an annulus, or "ring of fire."
option a: Meanwhile,
option b: For example,
option c: That is,
option d: Nonetheless,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The final sentence restates and clarifies what "annular" means, so "That is" fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? At many historic New York City parades—including the 1912 ticker-tape parade honoring US Olympic champions—the ribbon-like coils raining down were paper spools from "tickers," the telegraph machines once used to relay stock prices. ______ the tickers had long been out of use by the time of the 1994 parade for the New York Rangers. On that occasion, shredded ordinary paper added to the festivities.
option a: In addition,
option b: For example,
option c: Of course,
option d: As a result,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Of course" acknowledges the expected point that tickers were obsolete by 1994.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? In a 2022 study, Knut Bretzke and colleagues applied optically stimulated luminescence dating to gauge the age of stone tools unearthed at an archaeological site in South Arabia. The technique dates artifacts by measuring how much time has passed since the mineral grains in the surrounding sediments were last struck by sunlight. ______ the moment when the artifacts were buried stands in for the age of the artifacts themselves.
option a: In addition,
option b: For example,
option c: That is,
option d: Instead,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The final sentence restates the method's logic, so "That is" fits.

question: The student wants to explain what makes the neon sculpture glow. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Run Rush Run is a 1977 sculpture by Argentinian artist Margarita Paksa. It spells out the title phrase ("run rush run") in glowing blue, pink, and purple neon lighting. Neon lighting is made by heating glass tubes, molding them into shape, and filling them with gas. Passing an electrical current through the gas causes it to glow.
option a: An electrical current passes through the gas-filled tubes in Run Rush Run, making them glow blue, pink, and purple.
option b: A glow comes from Paksa's sculpture, which is built from glass tubes.
option c: The glass tubes of the sculpture were heated and molded to spell out the phrase "run rush run."
option d: Paksa's 1977 sculpture spells out the phrase "run rush run" in glowing blue, pink, and purple neon lights.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only option A explains the cause of the glow: an electrical current passing through the gas in the tubes.

question: The student wants to contrast the orbits of the two moons. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Saturn has 146 moons, including Hyperion and Prometheus. On average, Hyperion completes one orbit of Saturn in 21.28 Earth days. On average, Prometheus completes one orbit of Saturn in 0.61 Earth days. The German mathematician and astronomer Johannes Kepler (1571-1630) described planetary orbits as elliptical rather than circular. Kepler published three laws of planetary motion to describe how planets orbit the Sun. Kepler's laws apply as well to the elliptical orbits of natural satellites (such as moons).
option a: Saturn's moons Hyperion and Prometheus orbit their planet in the same way that the planets orbit the Sun.
option b: Hyperion's orbit of Saturn is elliptical and takes, on average, 21.28 Earth days, whereas Prometheus's orbit of Saturn is circular and takes, on average, 0.61 Earth days.
option c: Kepler's three laws of planetary motion describe the orbits of planets and of natural satellites, including those of Hyperion and Prometheus.
option d: Prometheus completes its orbit of Saturn many times faster than Hyperion does.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Option D contrasts the two orbital periods, noting Prometheus orbits far faster than Hyperion.
